children: Nifty IT index has fallen for the seventh straight session and is down more than 7 percent so far this month. Heavyweights including TCS, HCL Tech, Wipro and Tech Mahindra have declined between 5-10 percent during the period. The weakness comes after two consecutive months of buying in the sector.

The latest launches from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta are proving to be a double-edged sword for the sector. While better and cheaper AI models could accelerate enterprise adoption and create new revenue opportunities for IT companies, analysts fear that they also raise the risk of deflation in legacy services as more software and business processes become automated.
AI models are getting cheaper and closer in capability

Kotak Institutional Equities said the latest releases point to three important trends: software capabilities are improving, the gap between leading models is narrowing and vendors are increasingly focused on cost efficiency and cheaper pricing.
For Indian IT companies, this creates a mixed picture.

“Lower capability improvement in software-related tasks compared to certain other domains is a positive outcome for Indian IT,” Kotak said, arguing that it leaves room for more AI adoption by enterprises and creates new use cases for IT services companies.
At the same time, the brokerage said the deflation risk has not gone away. Even incremental improvements in coding and reasoning can add up as newer models are released.
Cheaper AI is a double-edged sword
The sharp fall in AI costs is another key factor for Indian IT.

Google and Meta are offering significantly cheaper alternatives, while Anthropic and OpenAI have also been working on improving price-to-performance. Kotak said lower costs should accelerate AI adoption, but this can work both ways for IT companies.

On one hand, greater AI usage can create new business opportunities for Indian IT firms. On the other, AI can automate parts of existing services, putting pressure on pricing and employee-intensive work.

Kotak therefore sees higher risks but also higher opportunities for Indian IT. It said companies will need to remain flexible and work with multiple AI model providers as the gap between models narrows.
The brokerage also flagged engineering and design services as an area to watch, given the improving capabilities of AI models.
AI revenue still too small to offset legacy pressure
UBS also sees both opportunities and risks, but said it is still too early to establish whether AI-related revenue can offset the pressure on traditional IT services.
AI revenues currently remain a small part of overall sector revenue, meaning investors cannot yet conclude that new AI-led growth will fully compensate for potential deflation in legacy services.

UBS remains selective and prefers Tier-2 IT companies over larger Tier-1 peers. It upgraded Tech Mahindra to Buy and raised its target price to Rs 1,865 from Rs 1,460, while downgrading HCLTech to Neutral from Buy. It also cut Persistent Systems to Neutral, citing valuation.

CLSA has taken a more cautious stance on large IT companies, downgrading TCS, Infosys and Tech Mahindra to Hold and Wipro and Mphasis to Underperform. It prefers mid-tier names such as Coforge and Persistent Systems.
CLSA said large IT companies face AI-led deflation in legacy managed services alongside macroeconomic headwinds, although higher AI volumes could eventually offset some of that pressure by FY30.

With valuations and expectations now being reassessed, the debate for Indian IT is increasingly shifting from whether AI is a threat to how quickly companies can turn AI adoption into new revenue before automation starts eating into existing businesses.

title: Nifty IT reverses 2-month buying streak as faster AI rollout renews deflation concerns
